task.instruction: How much does it cost to buy a 16-inch MacBook Pro with the highest-end Max chip Apple currently sells, in its standard memory and storage configuration? Name the chip and its CPU and GPU core counts.

final_answer:
The highest-end Max chip Apple currently sells in the 16-inch MacBook Pro is the **Apple M5 Max with an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU** (18-core CPU = 6 super cores + 12 performance cores; 40-core GPU, 16-core Neural Engine, 614GB/s memory bandwidth).

In its standard memory and storage configuration for that chip, that means **48GB of unified memory and a 2TB SSD** — per Apple's tech specs, the M5 Max with 40-core GPU is offered with 48GB, 64GB, or 128GB of memory (48GB is the base), and the M5 Max line starts storage at 2TB (2TB, 4TB, or 8TB).

On price: the 16-inch M5 Max entry configuration (18-core CPU / 32-core GPU, 36GB, 2TB) is **$4,399**. Selecting the 40-core GPU adds **+$300**, and Apple notes that this selection requires an upgrade to 48GB memory, which increases the total further. So the 40-core-GPU machine starts at **$4,699 plus the 36GB→48GB memory upgrade** — I was not able to confirm the exact all-in total on the page before running out of steps, so treat roughly $4,699 + the memory upgrade (a few hundred dollars) as the figure, not a verified final price. Note also that the 14-inch model offers an M6 chip, but the 16-inch tops out at M5 Max.

judge.rationale: The agent identified the chip, but did not provide a verified final cost; page state only shows $4399 for base M5 Max and +$300 unselected upgrade.
